definitions.explanation: A place other than here; elsewhere. Often implies somewhere unfamiliar or outside one's group.
People who are not part of one's own group or family.

examples.japanese: {余所|よそ}で{食事|しょくじ}しよう。
{余所|よそ}の{子|こ}と{比|くら}べてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't compare with other people's children.

examples.japanese: {余所|よそ}{見|み}をしないで{運転|うんてん}してください。
examples.english: Please don't look away while driving.

examples.japanese: ここがだめなら、{余所|よそ}を{探|さが}すしかない。
examples.english: If this place doesn't work out, we have no choice but to look somewhere else.

examples.japanese: {余所|よそ}の{家|いえ}のことに{口|くち}を{出|だ}さないほうがいい。
examples.english: You shouldn't meddle in other families' affairs.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}では{余所|よそ}{者|もの}はなかなか{受|う}け{入|い}れてもらえない。
examples.english: In this town, outsiders are not easily accepted.

examples.japanese: {余所|よそ}{行|い}きの{服|ふく}に{着替|きが}えてから{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I changed into my going-out clothes before heading out.

notes:
{余所|よそ} means 'somewhere else' or 'other people,' carrying a sense of separation — not part of one's own group, place, or concern.

WRITING:
Often written in hiragana as よそ. Also written as {他所|よそ}. The kanji spelling {余所|よそ} is common in dictionaries but hiragana is more frequent in everyday use.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {余所|よそ}{見|み}: looking away, getting distracted (especially while driving)
- {余所|よそ}{者|もの}: outsider, stranger
- {余所|よそ}{行|い}き: going-out clothes; putting on a formal front
- {余所|よそ}の{人|ひと}: other people, strangers
- {余所|よそ}の{家|いえ}: other people's homes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {他|ほか}: 'other' (more neutral, no connotation of exclusion)
- {別|べつ}の{場所|ばしょ}: another place (neutral)
- {余所|よそ} specifically implies 'outside one's own sphere' — unfamiliar, unrelated, or not one's concern
